summary: Quote on an NSE equity across two dropped sockets of a signed-in session: each reconnect connects with the market data session stored at sign-in, never logs in, and subscribes the book again whole, the instrument once in one request, so the next 1501 event reaches the client.

notes: Web #2484 (5749d4126): the feed connects with the market data token stored at broker login, read again on every reconnect (feed_token_provider), and never logs in while one is stored; a login of its own at /apibinarymarketdata cancelled the /apimarketdata session history uses. The corpus's 5paisa XTS module keeps the market keys in memory as a session does (tests/it/feed_corpus/xts.rs feeds_signed_in), so a login would show. Its stored token is shaped as XTS issues it, a JWT whose userID claim reads MD1_APP (tests/it/feed_corpus/fivepaisaxts.rs MARKET_TOKEN), so the case runs the web's path: the address takes the user id from the claim (market_data_user_id), where for a token without one the web logs in and the desktop connects with the user id XTS answered at sign-in (a declared deviation, families/xts/streaming.rs Connector::known_session).

Web #2504: the client keeps one entry per instrument, so a reconnect's replay never grows the book (test_replaying_the_book_on_every_reconnect_does_not_grow_it); the desktop's book is keyed by segment and instrument (families/xts/streaming.rs).
The third frame is made for this case from the second, a later trade.

deviations.reason: The web sends XTS's LastTradedTime as it comes, seconds since 1980-01-01 IST (1478686530 is 2026-11-09 10:15:30 IST): a wrong unit, since feed timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in milliseconds (1794199530000).
